S1_incident_reporting.quote: Manufacturers must report any thermal incident involving overheating, fire, injury, or material property damage to the relevant regulator within 24 hours of learning of it, with a preliminary account and known unit/model identifiers. The manufacturer must notify the affected owner within 72 hours of learning of the incident and provide safety steps; if a credible risk may affect other owners or nearby people, it must promptly notify those potentially affected and the regulator.

S2_thermal_testing.quote: A failure rate above 5% requires prompt regulator notification and a corrective-action plan with a defined retest schedule. The regulator may require further restrictions based on the evidence; exceeding 5% alone does not automatically prohibit sale.

S3_remote_shutoff.quote: New units placed on the market must support remote emergency shut-off, with safeguards against unauthorized activation and clear customer instructions. Manufacturers must retrofit already-installed units to support remote shut-off within six years of this standard taking effect, where technically feasible; they must provide owners a safe alternative and notify the regulator when a unit cannot be retrofitted.

S4_fire_suppression.quote: New units placed on the market must include built-in fire suppression beginning 36 months after this standard takes effect. Manufacturers must provide clear instructions on the system's operation, limitations, and maintenance.

S5_customer_disclosure.quote: A manufacturer must initiate a regulator-supervised recall and remedy process when any model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year. The manufacturer must promptly notify affected owners, regulators, and the public, and provide safe-use instructions pending the remedy. The regulator will determine the required remedy and whether affected units may remain in service or sales may resume after corrective action; the threshold requires a recall process but does not itself impose a permanent market ban.

document.section_notes: The final text is strong on reporting (24-hour regulator reporting for all thermal incidents, 72-hour owner notice) and on mandatory recall at 8 per 100,000, with no transition or corrective-action alternative. The weakest section is S2: the 5% failure rate triggers only corrective action and retest, with no sales stop and no transition limit, though per-model numeric results go to owners and purchasers without public publication. S3 and S4 sit inside the acceptable ranges (six-year retrofit with a safe alternative; built-in suppression at 36 months).
